Yes. uTorrent is installed on 2 of the 7 devices in initech-003, and both were installed during the last 30 days [I3JLKILKQTAC/2026-06-12, W2656QDAE2ZJ/2026-06-12].

**Evidence**
- **I3JLKILKQTAC** is a Mac mini (desktop, macOS 15.3) owned by emp-initech-1001 [I3JLKILKQTAC/2026-06-12]. uTorrent first appeared on 2026-05-29 and was not there on 2026-05-28. It's flagged as high-severity risky software (category: p2p_file_sharing) [risky_software/I3JLKILKQTAC/uTorrent, I3JLKILKQTAC/2026-05-28, I3JLKILKQTAC/2026-05-29].
- **W2656QDAE2ZJ** is a Dell XPS 15 laptop running Windows 11 22H2, owned by emp-initech-1004 [W2656QDAE2ZJ/2026-06-12]. uTorrent first appeared on 2026-06-02 and was not there on 2026-06-01. It's also flagged as high severity [risky_software/W2656QDAE2ZJ/uTorrent, W2656QDAE2ZJ/2026-06-01, W2656QDAE2ZJ/2026-06-02].
- The detector describes peer-to-peer clients as a common way for malware to get in and for data to leak out, and says they often break acceptable-use policy [risky_software/I3JLKILKQTAC/uTorrent].
- The same check also flagged TeamViewer on DARFCP0BQM2G (owner emp-initech-1000) at medium severity. It's a remote-access tool, which is fine if IT manages it but a takeover risk if the user installed it [risky_software/DARFCP0BQM2G/TeamViewer].

**Caveats**
- The data shows what software is installed, not what processes are running. I can't tell whether uTorrent is actually active on either device.
- I searched for the exact name "uTorrent". Other spellings, such as "µTorrent", would not have matched.
- I haven't proposed any actions because I don't have tools for that in this session. If you want to follow up, you could have the two owners uninstall it, or remove it through your device-management tool. You could also check whether IT approved the TeamViewer install.
